questions.q: What is affirmation, as Irwin describes it?
a: Strengthening people by focusing on their strengths and values
Rewarding results with bonuses and awards
Correcting mistakes quickly and privately
Setting clear targets for every employee
questions.why: Lesson 1 says affirmation means speaking in a way that fortifies others.

questions.q: What did the 2005 study find about affirmation?
a: It lowers stress and improves problem solving
It raises confidence without changing performance
It has little effect on adults
It only works in sports settings
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites the study's effect on stress and performance.

questions.q: Why is public criticism harmful, according to the summary?
a: It damages the brain's social reward connection and self-belief
It motivates others to avoid mistakes
It strengthens group cohesion over time
It is remembered only briefly
questions.why: Lesson 2 links peer rejection to lasting damage.

questions.q: How should a leader handle praise and criticism?
a: Give praise publicly and feedback privately
Give both publicly for transparency
Give both privately to avoid tension
Avoid giving either to stay neutral
questions.why: Lesson 2 says share praise in public and correct in private.

questions.q: What is wrong with number-based performance reviews?
a: They miss unmeasurable contributions and how work is done
They take too long to prepare each year
They favor junior employees over seniors
They reward teamwork too heavily
questions.why: Lesson 3 says reviews should focus on how a person works.
